```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 90)
# The evaluated examples run against a local replay of responses recorded from
# the production API (tests/testthat/fixtures/recorded, tools/record_fixtures.R):
# no network and no login at build time; the outputs are real API outputs.
soil <- soilhub:::replay_session()
```

```{r}
library(soilhub)
```

Many studies need only the **topsoil**: the first horizon of each profile.
This guide shows how to ask for it with `layer = "first"`, how to read the
column `first_layer_status`, and how the soil map units of SOTER and SOTWIS
are split into **components**. It assumes you have signed in as shown in
`vignette("soilhub", package = "soilhub")`. The outputs were recorded from
the Global Soil Data Hub API in October 2026.

## The first layer of each profile

With `layer = "first"` the hub returns, for each profile, only its first
horizon (or horizons, when several start at the same depth). Here: the WoSIS
profiles around Vancouver (Canada).

```{r}
vancouver <- c(-123.3, 49.0, -122.9, 49.4)
first <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", bbox = vancouver,
                           layer = "first", max_rows = 5)
nrow(first)
```

We asked for up to 5 rows and received 3: one row per profile, and there
are only three profiles with horizons in this box.

```{r}
first[, c("feature_id", "horizon_name", "upper_depth_cm", "lower_depth_cm", "first_layer_status")]
```

Each row is the first horizon of one profile. Two profiles start with an
organic F horizon (0 to 1 cm), one with a ploughed Ap horizon (0 to 20 cm).
All three have the status `surface`.

## What the status means

`first_layer_status` says how the first horizon was found.
`soil_first_layer()` lists the statuses the server can give:

```{r}
soil_first_layer(first)
```

In words:

- `surface`: the one horizon of the profile that starts at the soil surface
  (upper depth 0);
- `tie`: several horizons start at 0; all of them are returned (for example
  repeated samples of the same layer);
- `not_surface`: no horizon starts at the surface; the first available one
  is returned (look at its `upper_depth_cm`);
- `depth_missing`: SOTER only, the surface horizon has neither an upper nor
  a lower depth.

With `view = "revised"` (see `vignette("raw-vs-revised", package = "soilhub")`)
two more statuses can appear: `surface_within_5cm` (rule R2: a first horizon
starting within 5 cm counts as surface) and `first_mineral` (rule R3: the
first mineral horizon, below the organic layers).

You can count the statuses with `table()`:

```{r}
table(first$first_layer_status)
```

## Profile markings

The column `profile_markings` reports problems of the horizon sequence of
the profile in the source (SOTER profiles only; it is empty elsewhere). The
list of possible markings is in `soil_first_layer(first)$profile_markings`:

- `negative_depth_above`: an organic (O) horizon with a negative depth lies
  above the first horizon;
- `empty_row`: the first row of the profile is empty (no name, depth or
  value);
- `depth_order_conflict`: some horizons are not deeper than the previous
  one;
- `numbering_starts_at_N`: the horizon numbers (SOTER `HONU`) do not start
  at 1;
- `numbering_gap`: some horizon numbers are missing.

Here the profiles are from WoSIS, so the markings are empty:

```{r}
first$profile_markings
```

## Why a profile may return nothing

`soil_features()` lists the places (features) of a selection, even those
without measurements. Here we read the first three features of the same
box, with their coordinates as text (GeoJSON):

```{r}
places <- soil_features(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", bbox = vancouver,
                        with_geometry = "text", max_rows = 3)
places[, c("feature_id", "geometry_text")]
```

Is each of them among the profiles of the first-layer read?

```{r}
places$feature_id %in% first$feature_id
```

The first place has no row: it is a profile site without any horizon with
measurements in WoSIS, so a read of observations (first layer or all layers)
returns nothing for it. A profile can also return nothing with `layer = "first"`
when its first horizon has no value of the `variables` you asked for, or,
in SOTER, when its first row is empty.

## Soil map units and their components

SOTER and SOTWIS describe the soil of **map units** (polygons). A map unit
holds several soils, the **components**, each covering a share of its area
and represented by a profile. We read five horizons of the SOTER polygons:

```{r}
soter <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "soter_polygons", max_rows = 5)
soter[, c("component_rank", "proportion_percent", "is_representative", "suid",
          "horizon_name", "lower_depth_cm")]
```

The component columns:

- `component_rank`: the rank of the component in the map unit (1 is the
  largest);
- `proportion_percent`: the share of the map unit it covers (100 % here:
  these units have one soil);
- `is_representative`: `TRUE` for the component that represents the unit;
- `suid`: the SOTER unit identifier (SUID) of the map unit.

The upper depths of these SOTER horizons are missing in the source
(`upper_depth_cm` is `NA`): only the lower depth is recorded.

```{r}
soter$upper_depth_cm
```

Which components were returned? By default only the representative one:

```{r}
soil_metadata(soter)$components
```

## Choosing the components

The argument `components` chooses which components you get:

- `"representative"`: one component per map unit, the representative one;
- `"all"`: every component;
- `"cumulative"`: the largest components until their shares add up to
  `min_cumulative_percent`.

### A SOTWIS example near Tunis

SOTWIS map units have several soil components. We look at three SOTWIS map
units in a box near Tunis (Tunisia). First, the box:

```{r}
tunis <- c(10.0, 36.5, 10.5, 37.0)
```

`soil_features()` lists the map units without reading their horizons (here
with the shapes as text; `with_geometry = "sf"`, the default, returns them
as an `sf` object for maps if the package `sf` is installed):

```{r}
units <- soil_features(soil, datasets = "sotwis_polygons", bbox = tunis,
                       with_geometry = "text", max_rows = 3, progress = FALSE)
nrow(units)
```

Each of the three rows is one SOTWIS map unit (a polygon). The column
`components` holds, for each unit, a small table with its soil components;
here is the one of the first unit:

```{r}
units$components[[1]][, c("soil_code", "component_rank", "proportion_percent",
                          "is_representative")]
```

The first unit has a Gleysol (`GLe`) component covering 55 % of the unit; it
is the largest (`component_rank` 1) and represents the unit. Its horizons
are read with `soil_observations()`, asking for all the components
(`components = "all"`):

```{r}
sotwis <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "sotwis_polygons", bbox = tunis,
                            components = "all", max_rows = 5, progress = FALSE)
sotwis[, c("component_rank", "proportion_percent", "horizon_name",
           "upper_depth_cm", "lower_depth_cm")]
```

These five rows are the horizons of the first component, from 0 to 80 cm.
We stopped at 5 rows, so the other components of the unit are not shown:
raise `max_rows` to read them. The first horizon, D1, is listed twice with
the same values: the SOTWIS files of ISRIC carry a summary copy of the first
layer, and the hub keeps the source as ISRIC published it. With
`view = "revised"` the copy is hidden (rule R5, see the article on the raw and
revised views).

A few values of those horizons (SOTWIS values are estimates, not measurements):

```{r}
sotwis[, c("horizon_name", "clay_content", "organic_carbon", "ph_h2o")]
```

For a soil scientist: a SOTWIS polygon is a map unit made of several soil
components, each with a share of the area in percent, and the layers of a
component are **estimated** values for the representative soil, not
measurements of a profile at a site (`source_support` is
`"polygon_estimate"`). Here clay is 30 to 34 %, organic carbon decreases
with depth (from 10 to 3 g/kg) and the pH rises from 5.9 to 6.4.

### Other components

For example, all the components of the SOTWIS map units of Kenya, or the
largest ones covering at least 80 % of each unit (these calls are not run
here):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
all_components <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "sotwis_components",
                                    country = "KEN", components = "all")

main_components <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "sotwis_components",
                                     country = "KEN", components = "cumulative",
                                     min_cumulative_percent = 80)
```

You can combine `components` with `layer = "first"` to get the topsoil of
each component.

```{r teardown, include = FALSE}
soilhub:::replay_stop(soil)
```
